# ISSUE-282: registry transport boundary

Plan the operator-requested boundary-only split of #188: a dormant Linux Bubblewrap launcher and bounded inspecting HTTPS proxy. No adapters, node configuration, cache preparation integration, restore enablement, OCI, native Codex restore, authenticated registries, or host-cache replacement. Stop at the human plan gate.

## Dimensions and budget

Approved dimensions: multi_area / unknown / sensitive. Approved profile: investigation. This narrow implementation and validation should fit the total 16-hour claim budget. No profile change or further split is proposed. Estimate 12–16 hours including fixtures and validation; revisit at the human gate if the inspecting-proxy scope cannot fit this budget.

## What we know

- `internal/sandbox/executor.go:32` builds ToolExecutor commands; executorFlags at line 65 uses --unshare-all and existing cache semantics. Preserve both unchanged.
- `internal/sandbox/executor.go:166` implements CheckToolExecutor using its real launcher and a positive host-network control. Restore needs a separate probe rather than relaxing this offline probe.
- `internal/sandbox/executor_test.go:89` tests ToolExecutor boundaries; lines 249, 288 and 324 test cache reuse, validation isolation and discarded candidate writes. `internal/sandbox/toolchain_test.go:198` covers offline language commands.
- `internal/process/tree_unix.go:10` configures process groups; StopVerified at line 18 reports cleanup errors. A PID namespace is also needed against descendants creating another session.
- Makefile defines check as lint plus race tests. Compiled policy additionally requires go build and go test. Fragments live in changes/unreleased, including 270.md.
- Bounded reversible planning probe: `bwrap --unshare-all --die-with-parent --new-session --cap-drop ALL --ro-bind /usr /usr --symlink usr/bin /bin --proc /proc --dev /dev -- /bin/true`. Exit 1: “No permissions to create a new namespace”. /usr/bin/bwrap exists; presence alone is not capability. The probe modified no repository files.
- This snapshot lacks Git metadata: git rev-parse HEAD fails. New-file absence can be checked in the snapshot, but cannot be confirmed at the approved base here.

## What we're assuming

Native Linux .NET HTTPS clients support an HTTP CONNECT proxy and OpenSSL PEM trust; Maven and Gradle JVM clients support an HTTP CONNECT proxy and a Java truststore. These are concrete transport requirements here, to be verified with the planned protocol fixtures below; actual tool versions and configuration are operator review evidence. No ecosystem adapter is introduced. Approved source and repository cache ownership come from a trusted caller, not candidate-supplied paths. Structural safety is enforced here; future base selection and node policy integration are out of scope. Check these assumptions through the fake payload and root-containment tests before adding any production caller.

## Open questions

Actual namespace enforcement and descendant teardown require a capable Linux host. Operator has installed dotnet/Maven/Gradle toolchains for optional native-client review; this planner has not executed those clients. Protocol fixtures are implementation requirements, not deferred to #188. Verify PEM/JKS loading, proxy properties and ALPN fallback with those installed clients in operator review; adapters remain out of scope. Implement deterministic tests now, use precise infrastructure skips only for actual capability absence, and put capable-host execution in the PR review checklist. Do not block implementation on this host or live ecosystems. Recheck proposed new files against the coordinator-provided approved base in a Git checkout; if any exist, classify them as modified and reconcile before editing. Do not invent a base SHA.

## Decision artifact: native HTTPS through an inspecting proxy

The rejected custom fetch API is superseded. Implement the transport compatibility in #282, not #188. A native client speaks ordinary HTTP proxy CONNECT followed by TLS and HTTP/1.1, without knowing an internal fetch protocol. CONNECT establishes only a broker-terminated TLS session, never an upstream byte tunnel. GET/HEAD restrictions apply to decrypted registry requests, not to a replacement client protocol.

### Topology and bootstrap

Host broker (only component with outbound access) listens on a fresh per-run Unix socket. A small trusted helper runs as PID-namespace supervisor inside the same Bubblewrap network namespace as the payload. It listens on namespace-local 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port and forwards each accepted stream to that fixed Unix socket. It has no configurable destination, DNS capability or host-network namespace; bounded opaque forwarding is safe because the host broker interprets every stream. No slirp, veth, host-network fallback or route to an external interface is installed. The proxy is the only provided reachable network service; payload-local loopback sockets do not grant host or external access; direct external sockets and access to host loopback remain denied. The helper is killed with the PID namespace and cannot outlive the run.

Add a separate internal-purpose `cmd/swarm-restore-helper` executable, built explicitly in tests, not installed or wired into normal `swarm` flows. A trusted caller must supply its absolute, verified regular executable path; no PATH discovery or candidate helper. Mount it read-only at a fixed internal path. Helper starts the listener, sends readiness through a dedicated inherited control pipe, runs the boundary canary, and only then executes payload argv without shell interpolation. Its descriptor allowlist closes the control pipe and all unrelated host descriptors before payload exec. Missing helper, unavailable loopback or broken bridge makes capability unavailable before caller code executes. A direct payload connection to the exposed Unix socket gains exactly the same inspected proxy, never another protocol or authority.

The boundary supplies an ephemeral endpoint and read-only public trust files as its transport contract. For Linux .NET the contract is `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (also lowercase form), empty NO_PROXY/no_proxy, and `SSL_CERT_FILE=/restore-trust/ca.pem`, with SSL_CERT_DIR pointing to a synthetic empty directory. For Maven and Gradle it is JVM properties `https.proxyHost=127.0.0.1`, `https.proxyPort=<port>`, empty `http.nonProxyHosts`, `javax.net.ssl.trustStore=/restore-trust/ca.jks`, `javax.net.ssl.trustStoreType=JKS` and its public integrity password. These are native runtime settings, not new swarm CLI flags. Boundary exposes the endpoint/trust contract; adapter-specific Maven settings, Gradle invocation, dotnet restore commands and toolchain mounting remain out of scope. Tests pass the contract to fake clients. Ignoring it yields network failure, never fallback.

### TLS trust and certificate ownership

Create a fresh short-lived CA per run in host broker memory; its private key never crosses the namespace, appears in files/logs/argv, or enters cache. Pre-issue DNS-SAN server leaves only for exact approved hosts; keep leaf keys host-side as well. Leaves have serverAuth usage, bounded validity and random serials. Serve only TLS 1.2/1.3 with ALPN http/1.1 (or no ALPN for HTTP/1.1 clients); do not advertise HTTP/2. Native clients can negotiate HTTP/1.1; reject h2-only clients instead of relaying opaque frames.

Export only the public CA as PEM and a minimal trusted-certificate-only JKS v2 store, generated with Go standard-library encoding and tested against format fixtures. No Java/keytool prerequisite, persistent trust modification, or third-party crypto dependency. JKS password protects public-store integrity, not a credential. Mount trust artifacts read-only and disjoint from cache/source; remove on teardown. Upstream broker uses a separate system public-root pool, normal hostname/time/chain verification and no client certificates. The ephemeral interception CA is never added to upstream roots. Certificate pinning or clients that cannot consume this trust contract are unsupported and fail closed; never disable verification to accommodate them.

### Exact-host and virtual-host enforcement

1. Accept only canonical `CONNECT approved.example:443 HTTP/1.1` with matching Host. Normalize policy once to strict lowercase ASCII DNS names; no wildcards, suffix matching, IP literals, userinfo, percent-encoded authority, trailing dot, controls, whitespace, backslash, ambiguous ports or non-443 port. Refuse ordinary forward-proxy HTTP requests and all other CONNECT targets before any upstream dial.
2. Return 200 then terminate TLS locally. Require ClientHello SNI exactly equal to the CONNECT hostname; reject absent or different SNI, including another allowlisted host. Select only that host's certificate. CONNECT alone causes no outbound connection.
3. Parse each decrypted HTTP/1.1 request with bounded headers. Require exactly one Host equal to that pinned host (optional canonical :443), origin-form path, GET or HEAD, no request body, and no query/userinfo/fragment. Reject absolute-form, duplicate Host, conflicting lengths, transfer encoding, upgrades, nested CONNECT, WebSocket and malformed pipelining. Bind every keepalive request to the same CONNECT host; never honor a later authority change or HTTP/2 coalescing.
4. Reconstruct a new upstream HTTPS request using only the pinned policy host for URL authority, Host and TLS ServerName. Dial only validated numeric addresses. Never splice the inner stream or forward raw client headers. Thus a shared IP, SAN wildcard, domain fronting, different Host or second virtual host cannot escape the policy.

Resolve on every new upstream connection, reject the entire answer set if any address is unsafe, and pin the selected numeric IP without re-resolution. Deny loopback, private, link-local, metadata, unspecified, multicast, reserved/non-public and mapped IPv4 equivalents; IsGlobalUnicast alone is insufficient. Separate pools by exact host, disable ambient proxies, alternate protocols and automatic redirects. Rebinding tests cover changed answers on subsequent connections.

### Credential exclusion and native registry responses

Clear inherited environment and omit host home, credentials, Git, SSH agents, host caches and user package-manager configuration. Only detached approved source, the private cache, public trust and trusted runtime cross the boundary. Reject client Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, client-certificate attempts, authentication handshakes and credential-bearing/noncanonical URLs; never forward them. Rebuild upstream headers from a small validated allowlist: Accept, User-Agent (bounded printable value), Range, If-Range, If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since. Other benign native headers may be dropped; unsupported semantics fail closed. Strip connection-nominated and all other hop-by-hop headers. Unknown headers never pass through. Do not log raw URLs, headers, payload output or environment as broker diagnostics.

No request queries are accepted in this anonymous transport version; signed URLs and query-auth registries fail closed. Approved input must be credential-free; the broker cannot recognize an arbitrary secret intentionally encoded into an otherwise valid path. This boundary excludes ambient/authentication credentials rather than claiming content-level secret detection in approved source. Tests plant synthetic credentials outside approved input and assert zero upstream disclosure.

Forward bounded normal metadata/artifact responses, including Content-Type, Content-Length, ETag, Last-Modified, range and cache headers, preserving bytes. Do not decompress implicitly. Reject 401/407 and authentication challenges, Set-Cookie and protocol upgrades. Handle 3xx manually: accept only a credential-free HTTPS Location whose destination independently passes the exact-host policy; return it to the client without following it. A client's next connection/request must repeat all checks. Reject missing, malformed or disallowed Location before exposing it. Relative redirects resolve against the pinned authority; loops consume the same request/time budget. NuGet service-index resource URLs are not rewritten: each resource/CDN host must be explicitly approved, and any absent host fails closed. Maven/Gradle POM, metadata, checksum and artifact paths use the same contract, with no adapter implemented here.

### Bounds and lifecycle

Use internal constants, not bypass flags: CONNECT/header 16 KiB, response headers 64 KiB, URL 8 KiB, artifact 256 MiB, aggregate bytes 1 GiB, 1024 requests, 8 concurrent sessions, 16 accepted connections including pending handshakes, dial/TLS 5 seconds, request 60 seconds, run 5 minutes, teardown 5 seconds. Stream through bounded buffers; HEAD consumes no body; reject body overflow, framing errors, stalls and truncation. Bound helper queues and certificate count by the validated policy. Any policy/protocol/TLS failure cancels the whole run even when payload ignores the error. Ordinary 404 package-miss responses are allowed; payload exit status still decides run success. Close broker/helper listeners, both TLS legs, idle pools, active streams, goroutines and descendants before reporting completion. Discard failed output; no partial cache publication.

## Investigation outcome and review decision

The reversible namespace probe above confirms this environment cannot demonstrate the real launcher; it does not establish transport compatibility. Source inspection establishes that changing the existing offline executor would broaden current callers. Choose the separate inspecting proxy/helper design, with mandatory deterministic protocol fixtures and optional operator native-client evidence. Reject opaque CONNECT because destination TLS/HTTP cannot be checked; reject the prior custom fetch API because native clients do not speak it. The implementation decision remains contingent on independent human plan approval. No production probe, restore invocation or implementation was performed during planning.

## Exact files and symbols

Proposed new paths (verify absence at approved base; snapshot check recorded below):

- internal/sandbox/restore.go: RestoreRequest, RestoreBoundary.Run, CheckRestoreBoundary; narrow source/cache contract and lifecycle owner.
- internal/sandbox/restore_linux.go: restoreCommand, restoreFlags, same-launcher canary.
- internal/sandbox/restore_other.go: unsupported-platform error, no alternate executor.
- internal/sandbox/restore_broker.go: registryPolicy, parseRegistryTarget, resolveRegistryAddresses, registryBroker, serveRestoreConnect, inspectRestoreTLS, validateRestoreHTTPRequest, bounded handler and transport.
- internal/sandbox/restore_trust.go: newRestoreTrust, encodeTrustJKS; ephemeral CA and public stores.
- internal/sandbox/restore_helper.go: RunRestoreHelper; fixed-socket loopback bridge, readiness, canary and supervisor.
- cmd/swarm-restore-helper/main.go: internal executable entrypoint only; no ordinary CLI integration.
- internal/sandbox/restore_protocol_test.go: native CONNECT/TLS/HTTP transcripts, JKS and registry fixtures.
- internal/sandbox/restore_test.go: broker, policy, failure and lifecycle unit tests.
- internal/sandbox/restore_linux_test.go: real Bubblewrap fake-payload adversarial tests.
- changes/unreleased/282.md: prerequisite and dormant status, following existing fragment format.

Modify internal/sandbox/executor_test.go only if existing assertions need one focused offline regression assertion. Preserve production executor.go, native.go, validation.go, worker.go, dependency_cache*.go, node/CLI/configuration, protected harness files and docs unchanged. Only the internal helper command is added; no production caller or build/install integration is added.

## Implementation sequence

1. Recheck symbols and file absence in the approved checkout. Read internal/safefs APIs before creating input/cache/control paths. Use root-bound exclusive temporary creation and atomic replacement, rejecting symlink ancestors and special files. Never load policy from candidate source.
2. Implement the CONNECT/inspected TLS contract, public PEM/JKS trust generation, and bounded broker. Write deterministic native protocol transcripts first, covering NuGet index/resources, Maven metadata/artifacts and Gradle HEAD/range/conditional requests. Implement the fixed Unix-socket helper bridge and its supervisor; tests build its binary into scratch. No custom fetch API. Resolver/dialer test seams remain unexported; production always installs real filtering and verified TLS. Local TLS fixtures may map a validated synthetic public IP to a local listener inside the test dialer, never via a production bypass.
3. Materialize a detached approved-source snapshot of regular files/directories only, rejecting links, traversal, special files and nested Git metadata. Never bind a host checkout. Allocate a fresh private output under a trusted repository-owned cache root, disjoint from source, home, system and control paths. No existing host cache discovery or credential-bearing toolchain binds.
4. Build a separate minimal read-only runtime with /source read-only and only /cache writable for regular files. Necessary temporary files and synthetic HOME live under /cache. Expose minimal proc/dev interfaces, not host filesystem access. Enable only namespace-local loopback for the proxy helper. Mount only public trust and the trusted helper executable read-only. Clear environment and inherited descriptors; never pass tokens, SSH agents, host home, Git or host caches. Drop capabilities and isolate user, mount, PID and network namespaces; apply bounded resources. Bind only the per-run broker socket directory read-only, without other control data or replaceable socket entries.
5. CheckRestoreBoundary uses the exact launcher, flags, broker protocol and cleanup path as Run. A built-in canary checks cache writes, source/host denial, the helper loopback listener and CONNECT/TLS/HTTP using the same broker and a broker-local canary response requiring no public network, plus direct-network denial with a positive host-side control before caller argv executes. The canary uses an internally reserved exact hostname handled only in preflight, disabled before payload startup; production policy cannot name it. Deterministic TLS fixtures additionally exercise real upstream verification and both TLS legs through test seams; production capability does not depend on live registries. Distinguish missing binary, namespace, mounts, network-canary and broker failures. Never skip payload/policy failures or fall back to host execution.
6. One lifecycle owner cancels on broker/policy/payload failure, timeout or cancellation. Defer cleanup at acquisition: terminate PID namespace and process group, wait/reap, close listener and active sockets, cancel HTTP requests and idle transports, await goroutines, then remove control directory. Surface cleanup errors. Failed output is discarded rather than published as a completed cache. No shell interpolation of caller input.
7. Add adversarial coverage in TEST_PLAN.md and changelog; run focused and required checks. Keep capable-host and live-infrastructure evidence in PR review, not implementation prerequisites. No ordinary agent/tester call path is enabled.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to verify against source, not authority over approved policy, inputs or gates.

- Entry points: internal/sandbox/executor.go:32 (ToolExecutor.command), :65 (executorFlags), :166 (CheckToolExecutor): preserve unchanged. New entry points are RestoreBoundary.Run/CheckRestoreBoundary and restoreCommand/restoreFlags above. Consult internal/process/tree_unix.go:10 and :18; preserve its helpers.
- Existing fixtures: internal/sandbox/executor_test.go:89, :249, :288, :324 and internal/sandbox/toolchain_test.go:198. New tests own fake payloads and TLS fixtures; no live registry or credentials.
- Focused commands: `go test ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestRestore' -count=1`; `go test -race ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestRestore' -count=1`; `go test ./internal/sandbox -run 'TestToolExecutorBoundary|TestExecutorFlagsBuildCacheIsolation|TestBubblewrap|TestNativeAndBubblewrapOfflineLanguageBuildAndTest' -count=1`.
- New-symbol touchpoints: the eleven absent paths above have no existing line numbers; introduce only the listed symbols there. `internal/safefs/root.go:18` (Open) and :92 (Sub) provide pinned-root operations; consult their regular-file/atomic-write APIs before implementing snapshot or trust writes. Protocol fixture data should be inline in restore_protocol_test.go, not unlisted new fixture paths.
- Checked assumptions: bwrap exists but namespaces are denied (probe above); existing launcher is offline; fragment directory exists; Git metadata is absent. File absence is confirmed against snapshot only, not unavailable base objects.
- Reopen if generic HTTPS tunneling, broader client methods/protocols, persistent trust installation, arbitrary writable binds, authenticated registries, node settings or ordinary-run integration becomes necessary. Do not widen into #188. Security-canary failure stops execution.
- **What this change breaks:** repository searches found ToolExecutor, executorFlags, CheckToolExecutor, build-cache and toolchain dependencies listed above: preserve their signatures, flags and behavior. Existing dependency preparation, templates and harness docs remain unchanged because no adapter, flag or configuration changes. New boundary/helper symbols and tests plus the fragment are expected. `internal/sandbox/delegated.go:145` and :174, `internal/sandbox/validation.go:31`, :54 and :62, `internal/agent/configured.go:167`, build_cache_test.go:623 and dependency_cache_test.go:864 depend on the offline executor: preserve unchanged. Makefile build/install continues producing only swarm; helper is built explicitly by tests. No template, harness documentation or generated changelog updates are needed because no public invocation is enabled. Capability skips must not hide regressions. No generated CHANGELOG rewrite.
- Human gate: deliver planning artifacts only. Do not approve, implement, stage implementation or publish. Independent maintainer review is next.

Snapshot verification: all eleven proposed new paths were absent when checked individually. Approved-base verification remains explicitly unconfirmed because this snapshot has no Git metadata.

<!-- swarm:guidance:start -->
## Operator guidance

> Revise the rejected plan to address the operator human review: provide a concrete native dotnet/Maven/Gradle compatible HTTPS transport design while keeping adapters and activation out of scope. Custom GET/HEAD alone is insufficient; do not defer transport compatibility to issue188. No unrestricted CONNECT or host-network fallback. Explain trust/bootstrap/certificate handling if TLS inspection is used and how credentials and alternate virtual-host escape are prevented. Use protocol fixtures; installed live toolchains are available for operator review. Stop for human approval after planning.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->

# ISSUE-282 test plan

Tests below are planned, not executed results. Planning ran only the reversible Bubblewrap namespace probe recorded in PLAN.md. The human gate precedes implementation.

## Acceptance 1: dedicated source/cache boundary and adversarial denial

New tests use the TestRestore prefix in restore_test.go and restore_linux_test.go.

| Case | Concrete verification |
| --- | --- |
| Fake payload succeeds | Real launcher reads an approved fixture, uses native HTTP CONNECT, validates the broker leaf using the exported CA, then sends HTTPS registry requests through the helper loopback proxy against a controlled TLS fixture, and writes expected bytes only to its private repository cache. Assert source and external sentinels unchanged. |
| Home and credentials denied | Plant synthetic home/token/Git/SSH-agent/cache sentinels and hostile credential/proxy environment. Payload cannot read them through absolute paths, source links, proc parent-root or inherited descriptors. Assert tokens absent from argv, environment and diagnostics. |
| Input safety | Reject source symlinks, nested .git, traversal, special files and unsafe cache roots/ancestors before payload marker. Reject overlapping source/cache/control roots. |
| Read/write isolation | Payload source writes, outside-cache writes, socket replacement and path/symlink escapes fail. Cache output succeeds. Synthetic HOME and temporary regular files stay inside cache. |
| Direct networking denied | Positive host control is reachable; payload TCP/UDP IPv4/IPv6, loopback and metadata attempts fail while only its namespace-local proxy loopback and inspected Unix broker channel work; host loopback at a distinct port must remain unreachable. Do not accept ambient firewall failure as isolation evidence. |
| Exact hosts | Table tests reject nonallowlisted hosts, suffix/prefix lookalikes, wildcard policies, literal IPs and malformed authorities: userinfo, controls, whitespace, escapes, backslashes, encoded host, trailing dots, ambiguous/non-443 ports and non-HTTPS URLs. Assert zero upstream dials for rejected requests. |
| Address safety | Resolver fixtures cover every denied address class, mixed public/private answer sets, mapped IPv4, rebinding and repeated connections. Assert only the validated numeric address is dialed, without second resolution. |
| Virtual hosts and TLS | Controlled TLS server records expected SNI and HTTP Host. Reject mismatched Host/authority and inconsistent internal ServerName. Wrong-host, expired and untrusted certificates fail. A valid CONNECT is locally terminated and never relayed; reject raw tunnels, nested CONNECT, upgrades and inconsistent Host/SNI on every keepalive request. No upstream connection is opened for CONNECT alone. Reject forbidden redirects; allowed redirects return to the client and repeat all checks on the next request. The broker never follows them automatically. |
| Resource bounds | Exercise excessive headers/URLs/bodies, response and run aggregate limits, requests/concurrency/connection limits, stalls and truncation. Assert bounded completion, errors and cleanup. |

Commands: `go test ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestRestore' -count=1` and `go test -race ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestRestore' -count=1`.

Broker unit tests are deterministic with unexported resolver/dial seams and local TLS fixtures. Production TLS verification stays enabled; test trust roots remain local to fixtures. No public registry, package manager, credential or remote infrastructure is required.

## Native protocol fixtures: required by acceptance 1 and human finding

Add `TestRestoreProtocol*` in restore_protocol_test.go. These fixtures are automated implementation checks, not results already obtained. They must exercise the real broker parser and both TLS legs, not a mock fetch API. Drive the same transcripts over a test TCP-to-Unix bridge without Bubblewrap for unconditional unit coverage, then over the real helper in Linux integration tests. Resolver fixtures return synthetic public addresses; an unexported dial seam routes them to controlled TLS listeners. Production never admits loopback upstream or disables verification.

| Fixture | Required assertions |
| --- | --- |
| Native proxy bootstrap | HTTP/1.1 CONNECT host:443, 200, ClientHello SNI, exported-CA verification, ALPN http/1.1/no ALPN, encrypted origin-form request, bounded response; prove raw TLS never reaches upstream. TLS 1.2 and 1.3; h2-only refusal. |
| NuGet v3/.NET shape | Service-index JSON with PackageBaseAddress/registration resources, registration JSON, flat-container versions and nupkg download on separate explicitly approved hosts. Follow returned resource URLs without rewriting them. Missing CDN/resource host denied. Byte-identical package output in cache. |
| Maven shape | POM, maven-metadata.xml, checksum and JAR GETs, repeated reuse, normal 404 miss and allowed relative/cross-approved-host redirect. No local Maven repo, settings.xml, server credentials or cookies. |
| Gradle shape | HEAD followed by GET, conditional GET/304, valid range GET/206 and bounded chunked response; preserve metadata and bytes. Request and response framing exercised, not just URL parsing. |
| Trust bootstrap | Parse generated PEM/JKS v2 and verify expected CA DER, checksum and sole trusted-certificate entry against an independent known-format fixture. Verify leaf SAN/usage/time and per-run CA isolation. Optional installed JVM loads JKS; .NET loads PEM in operator review. No CA private key in mounted files, cache, diagnostics or payload descriptors. |
| Upstream trust separation | Valid system/test-fixture root succeeds; wrong-name, expired, untrusted and interception-CA-signed upstream certificates fail. No InsecureSkipVerify or client cert callback. No client mTLS negotiation. |
| Alternate virtual hosts | CONNECT A with SNI B (even both approved), absent SNI, SNI A with Host B, duplicate Host, second keepalive request to B, absolute URL B, host aliases sharing IP or wildcard certificate: reject, cancel and assert zero B dials. |
| Credentials | Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, Basic/Bearer, URL userinfo, queries including signed URLs, proxy auth, 401/407, Set-Cookie and credential redirects all fail closed. Hostile ambient proxy, token, HOME and JVM option variables never cross bootstrap. Unknown headers drop, sensitive headers reject; upstream recorder receives only reconstructed allowed headers. Broker errors omit raw request values. |
| Framing and limits | Partial CONNECT, TLS-before-CONNECT, oversized ClientHello/header, duplicate content lengths, TE/CL, request bodies, pipelining with authority change, malformed chunked response, upgrades, slow handshake, connection floods, byte/request/deadline exhaustion. Assert cancellation, no excess allocations/connections and bounded teardown. |
| Redirect/resource policy | Allowed HTTPS redirect returns Location without broker following; client follows through a fresh checked request. Reject HTTP, credentials, query auth, forbidden host and malformed Location before returning response. Relative Location remains on same pinned host. Loop exhausts bounded budget. |

Fixture values include normal NuGet, Maven and Gradle header sets to prove dropping unknown benign headers does not alter these transactions. Request range/conditional values are parsed and bounded. Test helper socket connection directly as well: bypassing its TCP listener must not bypass inspection. JKS encoding tests alone are not claimed as live JVM compatibility evidence.

Commands: `go test ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestRestoreProtocol' -count=1` and `go test -race ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestRestore' -count=1`. Fixture failures are failures even when Bubblewrap is unavailable; skip only tests requiring an unavailable namespace. No installed ecosystem toolchain is required by CI.

## Acceptance 2: same-transport capability, fail closed, teardown and checks

- TestRestoreCapability: fake missing Bubblewrap/helper binary, unsupported platform, namespace denial, loopback/listener failure, malformed helper readiness, trust-artifact failure, mount denial, broker startup failure, missing network restriction and failed positive network control. Each returns a distinct useful reason and leaves the caller payload marker absent. Inspect the real command builder so mocks cannot silently substitute the transport.
- TestRestoreCapabilityTransport: canary uses the production launcher, helper loopback listener, Unix socket, CONNECT, TLS, trust artifacts and decrypted HTTP. A reserved internal canary host returns a fixed broker-local response only during preflight, with no outbound connection; disable that handler before caller argv. Reject it from user registry policy and prove payload cannot reach it afterward. Fake payload fetch tests separately prove verified HTTPS through the same handler. Tampering with network isolation fails the preflight before caller argv.
- TestRestoreFailClosed: payload exit error, ignored policy rejection, malformed broker request, TLS failure, broker death, start/handshake failure, deadline and explicit cancellation all return errors; none invokes a host command or alternate network path. Partial output is not reported complete.
- TestRestoreCleanup: each failure point and success closes helper loopback and Unix listeners, accepted and upstream sockets and idle transports, joins goroutines, destroys per-run trust artifacts and removes socket/control artifacts, terminates/reaps descendants including background and new-session children, and reports cleanup failures. Use child markers, bounded waits and post-return connection attempts, not sleeps alone. Repeat starts/cancels under race detection to find leaks.
- Infrastructure absence may skip only actual Linux integration cases with the exact unavailable reason. Unit tests never skip; policy/payload failures are test failures. An unavailable run is recorded separately from a pass.

Run focused commands above, then the approved checks directly:

```bash
unformatted=$(gofmt -s -l .)
if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$unformatted"
  exit 1
fi
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go tool staticcheck ./...
go test ./...
make check
```

make check includes the full race suite. Record failures and environmental skips accurately; do not weaken tests or policy to obtain a pass. During implementation use approved scratch build caches if needed; no host-cache replacement or new configuration is part of this change.

## Acceptance 3: existing offline execution and dormant prerequisite

- Preserve and run TestToolExecutorBoundary, TestExecutorFlagsBuildCacheIsolation, TestBubblewrapAgentBuildCacheReuse, TestBubblewrapValidationBuildCacheIsolation, TestBubblewrapCandidateWritesDiscarded and TestNativeAndBubblewrapOfflineLanguageBuildAndTest.
- Check original executor flag assertions continue requiring --unshare-all, unchanged build/dependency cache mounts, and credential/environment isolation. Add one targeted regression assertion only if missing; never rewrite expected flags to accommodate restore.
- Review all new RestoreBoundary/CheckRestoreBoundary references: declarations and tests only; RunRestoreHelper may additionally be referenced by the isolated internal helper main. No ordinary developer/tester, agent/validator preparation, node, CLI, native Codex or cache-preparation caller. Search adapters/configuration to confirm no enablement or new flags.
- Verify diff contains only planned boundary files, internal helper command, optional executor test assertion and changes/unreleased/282.md. Fragment states dormant prerequisite and inspecting HTTPS transport without claiming ecosystem restore adapters are enabled. Include tests for the helper executable startup/control framing; build it explicitly into scratch before real-launcher tests. Existing docs/templates remain unchanged.

```bash
go test ./internal/sandbox -run 'TestToolExecutorBoundary|TestExecutorFlagsBuildCacheIsolation|TestBubblewrap|TestNativeAndBubblewrapOfflineLanguageBuildAndTest' -count=1
grep -R -n -E 'RestoreBoundary|CheckRestoreBoundary|RunRestoreHelper' internal cmd
git diff --stat
git diff -- internal/sandbox/executor.go internal/sandbox/native.go internal/sandbox/validation.go internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go internal/node internal/cli
```
